title: Cancer Mutation Simulator
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: college placement Biology
description: Interactive MicroSim demonstrating the multi-hit model of colorectal cancer showing how 6 sequential mutations in proto-oncogenes and tumor suppressor genes progressively disrupt cell cycle control

learningObjectives: Analyze how accumulating mutations progressively disrupt cell cycle control
Distinguish between oncogene activation and tumor suppressor loss
Explain why cancer requires multiple mutations over time
Identify the hallmarks of cancer contributed by each mutation
prerequisites: Cell cycle phases and checkpoint control

keyQuestions: Why do oncogene mutations require only one hit while tumor suppressors require two?
What happens to the growth curve as each mutation is added?
Why does cancer typically take decades to develop?
commonMisconceptions: A single mutation is sufficient to cause cancer
All cancer genes work the same way
Cancer cells grow faster than normal cells (they actually evade growth controls)
assessmentOpportunities: Predict the effect of each new mutation before clicking
Compare oncogene vs tumor suppressor mutation mechanisms
